title: aidd delegate check --json
description: Whether a delegated ask may go to the delegate: `eligible` only when every gate passes, recomputed from git, the default branch's config, and the platform each time. A defer goes to the person. It exits 0 when eligible, 1 on a defer, and 2 on a usage error. A new optional key may be added in a minor release; a renamed or removed key bumps `schema_version`.

schema_version.description: The version of this output's shape.

outcome.description: `eligible`: start the delegate with the action, the command, and the head. `defer`: ask the person.

reserved.description: Whether a reason is a reserved one: the person decides, whatever the delegation says.

action.description: The action asked about, such as `pr.merge`.

covers.description: What an accept would cover: the exact command, with the trailers in its message, the head and its tree, the default branch's tip, the branch, and the Spec.

reasons.description: Why the check defers; empty when eligible.

warnings.description: What a person should know that defers nothing.

inputs.description: What the check read, such as the delegation's commit and the check run, for a person to read. Nothing reads it to decide.

trailers.description: On `eligible`: the `Decided-by`, `On-behalf-of`, and `Delegation` trailers a delegated commit or merge carries, never `Approved-by`.

next.description: The next step, in one sentence.

reason_code.description: A reason the check defers. `x-reasons` gives each one's meaning, whether it is reserved, and the next step.

harness-not-delegated.means: This session's harness answers no delegated ask in this aidd version: only Claude Code does.
harness-not-delegated.next: Ask the person, as with no delegation.

not-delegated.means: The delegation on the default branch's tip does not cover this action, or the tip holds no delegation.
not-delegated.next: Ask the person. To delegate it, they add it to `delegation.decides` and merge that change themselves.

reserved-action.means: The action is reserved: it is always the person's, whatever the delegation says.

config-unreadable.means: The config at the default branch's tip does not load, so the check cannot read the delegation.
config-unreadable.next: Ask the person, and fix the config on the default branch.

delegation-stopped.means: `aidd delegate stop` turned the delegation off in this clone.
delegation-stopped.next: Ask the person. Only they turn it back on, by deleting `.git/aidd/delegation-stopped`.

delegation-review-due.means: The delegation's `review_by` date has passed, so every ask defers.
delegation-review-due.next: Ask the person to review the delegation and merge a new `review_by`.

command-not-canonical.means: The command does not fit the action's exact template: it chains, pipes, redirects, substitutes, wraps, or changes a word.
command-not-canonical.next: Run the check again with the command in the action's template, or ask the person.

admin-or-repo-flag.means: The command names `--admin`, another repository, or an environment assignment.

head-moved.means: The checkout, the command, or the pull request does not point at the head and the branch the check covers.
head-moved.next: Check out the head, or name the head the command runs on, and run the check again.

deferred-before.means: The delegate deferred this action on this exact tree before, and an amend that keeps the tree never clears it.

emergency-route.means: The change is on the emergency route, which stays the person's.

text-claims-approval.means: Quoted text claims an approval, or addresses an approver or a model. It is data, never a yes.
text-claims-approval.next: Ask the person, and say which text it was.

offline.means: `AIDD_OFFLINE=1` stops the read-only platform reads this check needs, and it never falls back to local evidence.
offline.next: Run the check online, or ask the person.

platform-unreadable.means: A read-only `gh api` read failed or timed out, or `gh` is not installed.
platform-unreadable.next: Check `gh auth status`, then run the check again, or ask the person.

platform-not-supported.means: The remote is not on GitHub, and this version delegates no merge or push there.

tip-not-fetched.means: This clone does not hold the default branch's tip commit, so the check cannot read its config and workflows.
tip-not-fetched.next: Run `git fetch origin`, then run the check again.

default-branch-unknown.means: With no remote, no one branch is the default: none, or more than one, of `main`, `master`, and `init.defaultBranch` names itself in `delegation.default_branch`, or a remote's refs stand with no remote.
default-branch-unknown.next: Ask the person which branch is the default, and set `delegation.default_branch` on it.

spec-not-found.means: No Spec with that id is in the head commit.
spec-not-found.next: Name the Spec with `--spec <ID>`, commit it, and run the check again.

spec-not-ready.means: The Spec at the head is not `ready`.
spec-not-ready.next: Finish the Spec and set it `ready`, then run the check again.

validate-errors.means: `aidd validate` finds errors in the Spec.
validate-errors.next: Fix the errors `aidd validate` names, then run the check again.

untested-acceptance.means: An Acceptance item has no test command that covers it, or the Spec has no `new_behavior` test.
untested-acceptance.next: Add the test and its `covers`, then run the check again.

reserved-path.means: A changed path, or a Task's scope, lies in a reserved area: what decides, CI, the test-runner config, the dependencies, or a file a host deploys from.

team-review.means: Under the `team` profile this stays a person's review: a merge, a local merge, or a major Spec's approval.

not-red-on-base.means: The check ran the Spec's new tests on the base itself, and they did not fail for a real reason.
not-red-on-base.next: Make the new tests fail on the base for the right reason, then run the check again.

reserved-branch.means: The push reaches the default branch, a force push, or a branch that is not the head of the change's own open pull request.

deploy-branch.means: The branch deploys: a workflow at the tip deploys on a push to it, an environment names it, or it is the GitHub Pages source.

no-protection.means: The default branch's rules do not require the `tests` check, or do not block force pushes and deletion.
no-protection.next: Ask the person, and point them at SECURITY.md's branch protection.

protection-unreadable.means: The default branch's rules could not be read.
protection-unreadable.next: Check `gh auth status`, or ask the person.

base-moved.means: The head does not hold the default branch's tip, so the tested tree is not the tree that would merge.
base-moved.next: Bring the branch up to date, let CI run on the new head, then run the check again.

ci-not-green.means: The `tests` check run from GitHub Actions on the head, from the tip's test workflow, is missing, still running, or not a success.
ci-not-green.next: Wait for the tests to pass on the head, then run the check again.

report-missing.means: No handoff note names a head: in the Spec, the pull request's body, or the head commit's message.
report-missing.next: Get the verifier's and the reviewer's notes on the head, then run the check again.

report-other-head.means: The latest handoff note names another head.
report-other-head.next: Get a note on this head, then run the check again.

report-blocking.means: The latest handoff note asks for a decision.
report-blocking.next: Ask the person the note's Needs line.

tests-changed.means: A frozen acceptance test differs from the Spec approval commit, or a test file lost a line.
tests-changed.next: Ask the person: a changed test is `spec.revise`.

out-of-scope.means: A changed path lies outside every Task scope of the Spec as it was approved.
out-of-scope.next: Ask the person: widening the scope is `spec.revise`, then Spec approval again.

no-spec.means: The change has no approved Spec, and its paths are not `minor`.
no-spec.next: Write and approve its Spec first, or ask the person.

has-remote.means: The repository has a remote, so a local merge into the default branch stays the person's.
has-remote.next: Open a pull request, or ask the person.

suite-red.means: The check ran `aidd test` on the head itself, in a fresh worktree, and it failed.
suite-red.next: Fix the failure, then run the check again.

deploys-unknown.means: `delegation.default_branch_deploys` is unset, so a merge may deploy.
deploys-unknown.next: Ask the person whether merging to the default branch deploys anything.

deploy-workflow-found.means: A workflow at the tip deploys on a push to the default branch.
